children: Iraq’s Ministry of Oil is implementing four associated gas capture and utilisation projects with a combined capacity of 1.4 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) as part of plans to end gas flaring by the end of 2029, the Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported on Sunday.
Ministry spokesperson Salim Al-Rikabi said the projects comprise Artawi, Bin Omar, Nasiriyah and Halfaya.
The Artawi gas project, the largest of the four, will have a capacity of 600 million standard cubic feet per day (mmscfd) and is being implemented in two phases.
The Bin Omar and Halfaya projects will each have a capacity of 300 mmscfd, while the Nasiriyah project will have a capacity of 200 mmscfd.
The ministry is separately working to utilise non-associated gas from the Akaz and Mansouriya fields to increase domestic gas supplies for power generation, industrial use and other applications.
In the downstream sector, the ministry is progressing projects to increase refining capacity and domestic production of petroleum products.

These include the Fluid Catalytic Cracking (FCC) project in Basra, which Al-Rikabi said is expected to produce around 5 million litres of high-octane gasoline and 10 million litres of gas oil for the domestic market. The completion ceremony of the Basra Refinery Upgrading Project, which included the FCC unit, was held in October 2025, according to a statement posted by the Japanese embassy in Iraq. The $4.8 billion project, financed by the Japanese government, is the largest yen loan project in the Middle East.
The ministry is also planning expansions at the Diwaniyah, Maysan and Najaf refineries, the INA report added.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
